title: Fourth Amendment and executive concentration
detail: Constitutional changes strengthened executive control and narrowed competitive parliamentary politics.

title: BAKSAL restructuring phase
detail: The state moved toward a one-party governing framework under BAKSAL, reorganizing political participation and administration.

title: Killing of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
detail: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was assassinated in a military coup, marking a violent rupture in Bangladesh's founding political order.

title: New power alignment after coup
detail: Post-coup authority was consolidated through rapid political realignment and institutional control.

title: Jail killing of four national leaders
detail: Syed Nazrul Islam, Tajuddin Ahmad, Mansur Ali, and AHM Qamaruzzaman were killed inside Dhaka Central Jail.

title: Counter-coup turbulence
detail: Competing military factions triggered successive upheavals, deepening instability in the chain of command and government.

title: Collapse of BAKSAL-era order
detail: The one-party arrangement collapsed amid violent transition, opening a prolonged phase of militarized politics.
